To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Observer pattern can be deprecate in favor of reactive dataflow programming by gradually migrating from the former to the latter.

(1) the observer pattern is a popular and widely used pattern in the context of reactive programming; (2) the observer pattern can be replaced by a declarative reactive programming style, which can be implemented by a dataflow DSL; (3) the dataflow DSL is implemented by an embedding into the host language using a continuation passing style (CPS) transformation.

(1) the Observer pattern is a common source of programming errors; (2) the reactive programming style is more expressive and less prone to programming errors; and (3) we have designed a gradual migration approach to help programmers migrate their existing observer-based code towards a more expressive reactive programming model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, implementation, and evaluation of a new approach to programming interactive systems that combines the benefits of reactive programming with the benefits of the observer pattern.
the design of programming languages and systems that enable programmers to build interactive applications in an efficient and declarative manner.
the following topics: • Designing a programming model for reactive programming. • Developing a high-level API layer for reactive programming.

we have developed a new approach to deprecate the observer pattern in favor of a reactive programming model, by providing a set of library layers that help programmers to gradually migrate existing code.
we have designed a new programming paradigm, called reactive programming, that allows programmers to write interactive systems in a more declarative style than is currently possible.
we have developed a tool chain that helps to gradually deprecating the Observer Pattern in Java applications in favor of reactive, declarative, and more expressive programming abstractions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to gradually depreciate observers in favor of a reactive programming model.
it is possible to deprecate observers and callbacks by means of an extensible higher order data flow DSL that is implemented as a transformation of the original code.
we can use a continuation-based embedding to provide a high-level DSL that is both powerful and safe.
